answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with bonded identity: each new agent burns an ember of stake and becomes a leaf in the juniper registry, a public tree no operator can rewrite. To earn rights it needs endorsements woven into a trellis of attestations from several already-bonded, independent peers. A Sybil attacker cannot mass-produce trusted names: each forged leaf needs its own ember plus k distinct honest endorsers, so minting m fakes costs m times the burn plus m*k bribes. Cloning one machine buys no votes without buying the whole trellis.
